  # Adversarial review: run-pipeline repair (commit 41190b6, HEAD~1..HEAD)
  
  Note on scope: the caller committed the working tree as `41190b6` ("pre-review checkpoint") while this review was opening, so the diff reviewed is `git diff HEAD~1 HEAD` plus that commit's four new files. Scratch copies only: `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-guidebook/908d973d-7650-4b6a-9ab3-eb41dc090acc/scratchpad/rev-scratch/` (`guidebook.db`, `rebuilt.db`, `main/` = `git archive origin/main`). Canonical DB sha256 `b4ab7888…` untouched; nothing in the project changed.
  
  ## Verdict
  
  Not mergeable as it stands. The refusals work and the migration reproduces, but the diff ships two gates that can pass having examined nothing or refuse legitimate writes: `db.py coverage` reports `complete: true` with zero required rows the moment the natural scope fill lands, and `log-search` now refuses every search scoped to ISO/INT/UN/HR/EU-in-English (ISO is in the P1 scope list; 3 live ISO searches already exist). Below that: `BLOCKED` in `v_scan_ledger` keys on all nine `processing_blocked_reason` values including `no-quantified-claims` ("read; carries no extractable value"), so a full reading is masked and reading debt is paid down by setting a reason that no verb can clear; the `--verify-authors` gate stops comparing bylines on any source whose payload repeats a name (demonstrated: a deleted co-author is not reported); the contract criterion `verified-reading` claims a corpus-wide reader for three clauses and the check reads one; `skill_vocabulary_audit` resolves `E-08`, `item_code`, `axis_code`, `population_code` as valid homes while flagging `DELETE` and `RES`.
  
  ## Problems, worst first
  
  **P1 — `coverage` passes with EXAMINED 0 after the scope fill the migration itself prescribes (HIGH).**
  `scripts/db.py:1066-1067`: `scope_recorded = any(r["scope_status"] ...)`; `required = in-scope rows if scope_recorded else admissible`. Migration `122_run_pipeline_repair.sql:14-18` says "NULL = not yet recorded" and the ledger (OR-12a) says "Arabic, Bengali, Hindi and Swahili are scoped out". The natural data PR marks those four `scoped-out` and leaves the rest NULL. Then every slug is complete with nothing searched.
  ```
  # scratch copy only
  UPDATE lang_jur_map SET scope_status='scoped-out' WHERE language IN ('AR','BN','HI','SW');  -- then db.get_coverage_completeness(slug)
  → {'jurisdictions_searched': 0, 'jurisdictions_required': 0, 'languages_searched': 0, 'languages_required': 0, 'scope_recorded': True, 'complete': True}
  ```
  Before the fill: `jurisdictions_required 31, languages_required 19`. Test G02 (`test_run_pipeline_refusals.py:436-438`) asserts `scope_recorded is False`, so the test goes red on the legitimate data PR and green on this failure.
  
  **P2 — `log-search` refuses every search scoped to a jurisdiction the map does not pair, including P1's ISO (HIGH).**
  `scripts/db.py:864-872`. `lang_jur_map` has no row for ISO, INT, UN, HR, UG (the adjudication's own RC-H names them) and pairs FI with FI/SV, NO with NO, KR with KO. `workplan/2026-10-30-ramp-spec-pages/HANDOFF.md:61` lists ISO and EU in P1.
  ```
  db.log_search(slug=<active>, language='EN', jurisdiction='ISO', ..., dry_run=True)
  → REFUSAL: --language EN with --jurisdiction ISO: lang_jur_map pairs ISO with no language at all ... omit --jurisdiction
  select jurisdiction,count(*) from search_executions where jurisdiction in ('ISO','INT','UN','EU') → EU 2, INT 2, ISO 3, UN 2
  select distinct language from search_executions where language not in (select language from lang_jur_map) → nl, fr, HR, en, ja
  ```
  The refusal conflates "which bucket member a search counts toward" (OR-8) with "which searches may be logged" (R8: log every query). The skill's remedy is to omit `--jurisdiction`, i.e. drop a fact to get the row in. Also case: lower-case `en`/`fr`/`nl` live rows are now unloggable shapes (the test was changed from `en` to `EN` to pass).
  
  **P3 — `BLOCKED` treats all nine `processing_blocked_reason` values as "cannot be read", masks a full reading, and nothing can clear it (HIGH).**
  `122_run_pipeline_repair.sql:143` (`WHEN b.processing_blocked_reason IS NOT NULL THEN 'BLOCKED'`, above READ-NOTHING-FOUND); `scripts/migrations/057_baseline_2026-08-12.sql:300` defines `'no-quantified-claims' -- read; carries no extractable value`; also `out-of-scope`, `tier-not-required`, `superseded`. `scan_debt.py:41` excludes BLOCKED from debt; `research_batch_dod.py` R16-scan `live_adm` excludes blocked admissions.
  ```
  # scratch: REF-00139 before: [('EXTRACTED', 6), ('READ-NOTHING-FOUND', 4)]
  UPDATE evidence_sources SET processing_blocked_reason='no-quantified-claims' WHERE ref_id='REF-00139'
  after: [('BLOCKED', 4), ('EXTRACTED', 6)]
  'processing_blocked_reason' in db._AMENDABLE → False ; record_scan has no refusal on a blocked source
  ```
  `add-source --processing-blocked-reason` is now the only writer; no verb clears it ("until the block clears" has no path), and `add-source` accepts it alongside `VERIFIED`.
  
  **P4 — `--verify-authors` (check `author_fidelity`, `check-registry.yaml:594-611`, advisory) no longer compares bylines on a MALFORMED payload (MEDIUM-HIGH, 5(c) class).**
  `scripts/research/retrieval_log.py:1886-1892`: `if repeated: malformed.append(...)` `elif _author_conflict(real, stored)`. The elif suppresses the stored-vs-payload diff for exactly the sources with messy deposits.
  ```

  author-cross line present: False | MALFORMED reported: True | payload human authors: 6, stored: 5
  ```
  The payload's human authors (entries with `family`) are unambiguous after dropping the `name`-only repeats; the comparison could run on those.
  
  **P5 — Contract criterion claims a reader it does not have (MEDIUM).**
  `governance/pipeline-contract.yaml:213-224` `verified-reading`: "...and no extraction exists for a source that is not VERIFIED or for a (source, parameter) no reading covers ... the corpus-wide reader is the check below". `verified_scan_integrity.py` examines only `extraction_status='verified'` rows (EXAMINED 31).
  ```
  select count(*) from source_value_extractions x join evidence_sources e using(ref_id) where coalesce(e.verification_status,'')<>'VERIFIED' → 12
  extractions with no covering source_scans row → 105 (of 214)
  ```
  No check reports either population; the writer refusal is the only enforcement and the contract says otherwise.
  
  **P6 — `skill_vocabulary_audit` is green on the tokens CLAUDE.md §7 poisons and red on English words (MEDIUM).**
  `scripts/audit/skill_vocabulary_audit.py:49-136` builds `homes` from every quoted lowercase string in every audit script, every CLAUDE.md backtick, every tracked filename (12,867 tokens).
  ```
  homes(conn) membership: item_code=True, E-08=True, population_code=True, axis_code=True, contested=True
                          mode_s_trigger=False, SPECULATIVE=False, CROSS-ITEM=False, DELETE=False, VIS=False

  ```
  Red by construction on 18 files from birth (rule 6's argument), and the registry note (`check-registry.yaml:630-650`) says "The three skills /run-pipeline delegates to are the ones this change cleaned" while the output lists `cross-population-conflict-mapper_SKILL.md: DBL, MCAS, NEU, OFS, POTS, SENS, VIS` and the adjudication §5 P says they "stay reported". "Three" is a hand-typed count; run-pipeline names many more delegates.
  
  **P7 — A9 fixed as a parity refusal, not a derivation; rule 8's named anti-pattern (MEDIUM).**
  `scripts/db.py:3880-3887` and `:10445-10450` refuse any `--ref-id` that is not `next_ref_id` (or locator-staged), while argparse keeps `--ref-id` `required=True` for `add-source` and `add-locator`:
  ```
  python3 scripts/db.py add-source --title t ... --session S --dry-run → error: the following arguments are required: --ref-id
  ```
  CLAUDE.md rule 8 lists `add-source --ref-id` as the outstanding violation ("a field that can only be right or wrong, never informative"). `add-connection --con-id` took the right route (optional, computed); the two ref_id writers took the opposite one in the same diff.
  
  **P8 — Architecture doc edited in the hunk and left wrong on the adjacent line (MEDIUM, rule 4 prose caller).**
  `architecture/sqlite-data-layer.md:140` now says `CHECK(confidence IN ('HIGH','MODERATE'))` with a migration-122 comment; `:142` still lists `'CROSS-POPULATION','CROSS-ITEM'` for `connection_type`. Same file `:541` still documents `next-id connections|gaps|terms`. `scripts/db.py:20` usage header still shows `add-connection --con-id CON-0001`.

  **P11 — `set-parameter-direction contested` now requires one source's extraction (MEDIUM; doctrinal, withheld).**
  `skills/cross-population-conflict-mapper_SKILL.md:229` still prescribes `set-parameter-direction contested`; `db.py:6756-6778` refuses without `--ref-id` holding an extraction for the parameter. A contested direction is a cross-source judgment; OR-21 (project-standards.md:4721, "when it first arises") records a direction per lens. The skill line names a path the writer now refuses.
  ```

  ```

  `scripts/db.py:162-167` keys a hand-maintained dict on `connection_type` CHECK values; `:215` `.get(ctype, (None, 0))` means a type absent from the dict passes with any arity, while the comment says "add-connection refuses it by name". Unreachable today (the dict matches the four CHECK values; `None` is refused by `check_declared`).

  `CLAUDE.md:433` "`conflicts.item_code` survives as a plain column" — `PRAGMA table_info(conflicts)` has no `item_code` (migration 121). `workplan/pipeline-state-graph/CAPABILITIES.md:104` / `capabilities.yaml:98` "no column can name a parameter" for conflicts. `verified_scan_integrity`'s registry note names "the render contract (C5)" as its reader — a draft document, not a reader (§8 "name what reads it").

# Adversarial review: run-pipeline repair (commit 41190b6, HEAD~1..HEAD)

Note on scope: the caller committed the working tree as `41190b6` ("pre-review checkpoint") while this review was opening, so the diff reviewed is `git diff HEAD~1 HEAD` plus that commit's four new files. Scratch copies only: `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-guidebook/908d973d-7650-4b6a-9ab3-eb41dc090acc/scratchpad/rev-scratch/` (`guidebook.db`, `rebuilt.db`, `main/` = `git archive origin/main`). Canonical DB sha256 `b4ab7888…` untouched; nothing in the project changed.

## Verdict

Not mergeable as it stands. The refusals work and the migration reproduces, but the diff ships two gates that can pass having examined nothing or refuse legitimate writes: `db.py coverage` reports `complete: true` with zero required rows the moment the natural scope fill lands, and `log-search` now refuses every search scoped to ISO/INT/UN/HR/EU-in-English (ISO is in the P1 scope list; 3 live ISO searches already exist). Below that: `BLOCKED` in `v_scan_ledger` keys on all nine `processing_blocked_reason` values including `no-quantified-claims` ("read; carries no extractable value"), so a full reading is masked and reading debt is paid down by setting a reason that no verb can clear; the `--verify-authors` gate stops comparing bylines on any source whose payload repeats a name (demonstrated: a deleted co-author is not reported); the contract criterion `verified-reading` claims a corpus-wide reader for three clauses and the check reads one; `skill_vocabulary_audit` resolves `E-08`, `item_code`, `axis_code`, `population_code` as valid homes while flagging `DELETE` and `RES`.

## Problems, worst first

**P1 — `coverage` passes with EXAMINED 0 after the scope fill the migration itself prescribes (HIGH).**
`scripts/db.py:1066-1067`: `scope_recorded = any(r["scope_status"] ...)`; `required = in-scope rows if scope_recorded else admissible`. Migration `122_run_pipeline_repair.sql:14-18` says "NULL = not yet recorded" and the ledger (OR-12a) says "Arabic, Bengali, Hindi and Swahili are scoped out". The natural data PR marks those four `scoped-out` and leaves the rest NULL. Then every slug is complete with nothing searched.
```
# scratch copy only
UPDATE lang_jur_map SET scope_status='scoped-out' WHERE language IN ('AR','BN','HI','SW');  -- then db.get_coverage_completeness(slug)
→ {'jurisdictions_searched': 0, 'jurisdictions_required': 0, 'languages_searched': 0, 'languages_required': 0, 'scope_recorded': True, 'complete': True}
```
Before the fill: `jurisdictions_required 31, languages_required 19`. Test G02 (`test_run_pipeline_refusals.py:436-438`) asserts `scope_recorded is False`, so the test goes red on the legitimate data PR and green on this failure.

**P2 — `log-search` refuses every search scoped to a jurisdiction the map does not pair, including P1's ISO (HIGH).**
`scripts/db.py:864-872`. `lang_jur_map` has no row for ISO, INT, UN, HR, UG (the adjudication's own RC-H names them) and pairs FI with FI/SV, NO with NO, KR with KO. `workplan/2026-10-30-ramp-spec-pages/HANDOFF.md:61` lists ISO and EU in P1.
```
db.log_search(slug=<active>, language='EN', jurisdiction='ISO', ..., dry_run=True)
→ REFUSAL: --language EN with --jurisdiction ISO: lang_jur_map pairs ISO with no language at all ... omit --jurisdiction
select jurisdiction,count(*) from search_executions where jurisdiction in ('ISO','INT','UN','EU') → EU 2, INT 2, ISO 3, UN 2
select distinct language from search_executions where language not in (select language from lang_jur_map) → nl, fr, HR, en, ja
```
The refusal conflates "which bucket member a search counts toward" (OR-8) with "which searches may be logged" (R8: log every query). The skill's remedy is to omit `--jurisdiction`, i.e. drop a fact to get the row in. Also case: lower-case `en`/`fr`/`nl` live rows are now unloggable shapes (the test was changed from `en` to `EN` to pass).

**P3 — `BLOCKED` treats all nine `processing_blocked_reason` values as "cannot be read", masks a full reading, and nothing can clear it (HIGH).**
`122_run_pipeline_repair.sql:143` (`WHEN b.processing_blocked_reason IS NOT NULL THEN 'BLOCKED'`, above READ-NOTHING-FOUND); `scripts/migrations/057_baseline_2026-08-12.sql:300` defines `'no-quantified-claims' -- read; carries no extractable value`; also `out-of-scope`, `tier-not-required`, `superseded`. `scan_debt.py:41` excludes BLOCKED from debt; `research_batch_dod.py` R16-scan `live_adm` excludes blocked admissions.

after: [('BLOCKED', 4), ('EXTRACTED', 6)]
'processing_blocked_reason' in db._AMENDABLE → False ; record_scan has no refusal on a blocked source
```
`add-source --processing-blocked-reason` is now the only writer; no verb clears it ("until the block clears" has no path), and `add-source` accepts it alongside `VERIFIED`.

**P4 — `--verify-authors` (check `author_fidelity`, `check-registry.yaml:594-611`, advisory) no longer compares bylines on a MALFORMED payload (MEDIUM-HIGH, 5(c) class).**
`scripts/research/retrieval_log.py:1886-1892`: `if repeated: malformed.append(...)` `elif _author_conflict(real, stored)`. The elif suppresses the stored-vs-payload diff for exactly the sources with messy deposits.

`governance/pipeline-contract.yaml:213-224` `verified-reading`: "...and no extraction exists for a source that is not VERIFIED or for a (source, parameter) no reading covers ... the corpus-wide reader is the check below". `verified_scan_integrity.py` examines only `extraction_status='verified'` rows (EXAMINED 31).

```
No check reports either population; the writer refusal is the only enforcement and the contract says otherwise.

**P6 — `skill_vocabulary_audit` is green on the tokens CLAUDE.md §7 poisons and red on English words (MEDIUM).**

`scripts/db.py:3880-3887` and `:10445-10450` refuse any `--ref-id` that is not `next_ref_id` (or locator-staged), while argparse keeps `--ref-id` `required=True` for `add-source` and `add-locator`:

Live CHECK: `['COMPOUND-INTERACTION','CROSS-PARAMETER','CROSS-POPULATION','METHODOLOGY']`. `CROSS-ITEM` is retired item-layer vocabulary. `test_run_pipeline_refusals.py:353` `res == "CON-0001"` (red when the first real connection lands); `:436-438` `scope_recorded is False` and `jurisdictions_required <= 48` (48 is a typed literal; the comment at `db.py:1051-1052` records 48 as the number a stale dashboard once used). `:129` and `:373` hard-code `MOB` and `LIGHT-INT` under a comment saying nothing is hard-coded.

The skill's remedy is to omit `--jurisdiction`, which drops a fact to get the row in. This conflates "which bucket a search counts toward" with "which searches may be logged", and R8 says to log every query.
3. **`BLOCKED` ledger state masks real readings.** It keys on all nine `processing_blocked_reason` values, including `no-quantified-claims`, whose CHECK comment reads "read; carries no extractable value". Setting that on REF-00139 turned its 4 READ-NOTHING-FOUND pairs into BLOCKED, and no verb clears the column.

For every R2 ID: PATCH, OWNER DECISION, or NO ACTION, with the reason. Apply the section 8 order (do nothing and say why; change a rule or convention; reuse what exists; delete the cause; only then the smallest added code), and enforce at the lowest layer that can hold a rule. Take particular care with these, where round 1 chose a path the reviewers dispute:
 - R2-1/R2-2/R2-14 and owner question 5: decide how `coverage`, `v_coverage_priority`, `lang_jur_map.scope_status` and `log-search`'s pair check should relate so that "what is owed" has ONE home, a requirement can never fall to zero because a column is partly filled, and every query is still loggable (R8).  - R2-16: the vocabulary check must be able to go red on retired or poisoned tokens (`item_code`, `E-08`, `axis_code`, `population_code`) and must not be red by construction on English words in prose; define the homes from the schema and the verb/flag/check inventories, not from every quoted string in the tree; replace the hand-typed "three" with a computed statement or delete the sentence. Decide whether the check belongs in the registry as advisory or should not exist (section 8: state what wrong thing reaches the guidebook without it).
 - R2-15: either make the criterion's wording match what the check reads, or extend the reader; justify with section 8.
Also apply the vocabulary and terminology requirement from the user: every value or flag a skill, help text or refusal names must be derived from the live schema or the verb inventory, terms must match project doctrine (ICF codes with names, no bare axis codes or population umbrellas, no item-layer codes treated as containers, tier and marker vocabulary per governance/tier-system.md), and prose must match the flag it cites. Canadian English in prose you write or specify.
Respect rule 10 (tooling only; no research rows; no hand SQL into the DB), rule 3 (any schema change is a numbered migration after 122, re-check the highest number when you write it, verified with `migrate_db.py --rebuild`), and rule 4 (sweep callers with `grep -r` or `git grep`, not the Grep tool). `repo-sweep` and `db-census` agents exist but you cannot call them; do the sweeps with Bash.

OUTPUT
Write /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-guidebook/908d973d-7650-4b6a-9ab3-eb41dc090acc/scratchpad/run-pipeline-round2-adjudication.md with: (1) a disposition table for every R2 ID; (2) the owner questions, each one clear question with the options and consequences, including the carried ones; (3) executor briefs, one per patch unit, in the order they must run. Each brief is self-contained for a Sonnet executor who has not seen this conversation: the IDs it closes; the exact files it may touch (disjoint across units that can run in parallel; units sharing a file, and every migration, are sequential and say so); the change in plain terms with the reasoning an executor needs; what the added code reads, what wrong thing it prevents, what it makes deletable; the acceptance test, which must be shown failing on the current tree and passing after, written so that it cannot go red on legitimate future data (no typed counts, ids or codes it could derive); the vocabulary derivations to use; and the checks to run. Executors edit the working tree only (no commit, no push, no PR, no canonical-DB write except through `migrate_db.py`) and test on a scratch copy of the DB. Include a final verification brief for an independent replay agent (the same usability-review framing as before, plain wording, commands and results only) covering every PATCH ID in both directions: the wrong write refused with a message that names the rule and the correct flag, and the valid write beside it still accepted.
Your final message to me: the disposition table in compact form, the owner questions, the ordered list of unit names with the files each owns, and anything you could not reproduce or decide. Report plainly; do not claim a ruling you did not check against the code.

Fable's round-2 adjudication is done, and I've dispatched the first Sonnet executor, Unit M (migration 123). The units run in the order Fable set, because each depends on files or a migration from the one before.

**Fable's round-2 dispositions** (all PATCH except as noted; it reproduced every finding and marked none NOT REPRODUCED):
- **R2-1:** a new view `v_research_scope` becomes the one home for "what is owed". `v_coverage_priority` and `coverage` both read it, and `complete` is false whenever the requirement is empty.
- **R2-2:** delete `log-search`'s pair refusal, since live rows already hold pairs outside the map. Keep the language-in-map and jurisdiction-enum checks.
- **R2-3:** only five of the nine `processing_blocked_reason` values mean "could not be read" (`no-full-text`, `paywalled`, `no-doi`, `not-indexed`, `language`). A reading outranks a block, and `record-scan` clears the column. `out-of-scope` and `tier-not-required` become owner question 8.
- **R2-4:** compare stored authors against the payload's family-named authors even when a name repeats.
- **R2-5:** refuse `full` on a text with no pages when the source's own Crossref payload states a page range.
- **R2-6:** `observe-term` never called the exempt-with-body refusal. It will reuse it, and the derived-text detection now reads the manifest flag rather than a `-full-text.txt` suffix.
- **R2-9:** `--ref-id` becomes optional and derived, like `--con-id`.
- **R2-16:** the vocabulary check stays advisory, with homes taken from the schema and the verb, flag and check inventories. `item_code`, `axis_code`, `population_code` and `E-08` stop resolving, and the "three skills" sentence goes.
- **R2-17:** `governing_refs` can't be dropped, because twelve data migrations insert it. The skill will point at `v_determination_provenance.role` instead.
- **R2-8:** an owner decision, with no code change before you answer.

**New owner questions, added to the six carried:**
- **Q7 (contested direction):** does it need one source per side, no source, or one source? Should parameters 3 and 12's NULL `direction_ref_id` be backfilled by a compensating migration or left as history?
- **Q8 (blocked reasons):** retire `out-of-scope` and `tier-not-required`, exempt them from reading, or annotate only?
- **Q5, restated:** the 17 map-only jurisdictions. Until you answer, `coverage` reports `complete: false` on every slug, and the cause shows as `jurisdictions_unreachable`. Fable chose an honest red over a pass that couldn't be attained.

**Run order**

| Step | Unit | Files it owns |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | M (running) | migration 123, `data/guidebook.db` via migrate, `governance/context-map.yaml` |
| 2 | R and C, in parallel | R: `scripts/research/retrieval_log.py`. C: the audits, `assess_cell.py`, the check registry, the contract |
| 3 | A1 | `scripts/db.py` |
| 4 | A2 | `scripts/db.py` (after A1) |
| 5 | T | `scripts/tests/test_run_pipeline_refusals.py` |
| 6 | P | the three skills, `architecture/sqlite-data-layer.md`, two `CLAUDE.md` sentences, `capabilities.yaml` and its rendered outputs, `_template.md` and its attestation |
| 7 | V | independent replay, writes only to the scratchpad |

After V comes a second antagonist pass over the whole diff. Four caveats from Fable's report:
- The obstacle classification is its reading of the CHECK comments, so the review should test it.
- Treating an article-number-only deposit as not paged is deliberate.
- The slug writer and the `supersede_source` parser name were not confirmed, so the executors derive both.
- Six legacy UNVERIFIED sources need a data PR, and that stays out of this one.

I'll relay each unit's result as it reports, and commit at the next natural break.

**Unit A1 results.** Only `scripts/db.py` changed, and the canonical DB's sha256 is the same before and after. The acceptance script has 20 cases: it fails 16 of the 19 that run on the old code and passes all 20 on the new. The three that pass on old code are the "legitimate shape still lands" cases. Four cases (B10, B11, I12, I13) go red on the old code only because of the "omit --ref-id" wording or the missing flag, and G12 cannot go red there because the old code has no `pairs_searched` key. Details:
- **`coverage`:**
  - New keys are `pairs_required`, `pairs_searched`, `pairs_unsearched`, `jurisdictions_unreachable` and `searches_outside_scope`.
  - `scope_recorded` is gone, and `complete` is false whenever nothing is required or something is unsearched.
  - A MERGED slug (`hearing-impairment-built-environment`) with no searches showed `searched 70/70, complete true` under the brief's `searched = required − unsearched`, so the executor changed `pairs_searched` to be read from the search log. It is now `0, complete false`.
- **`log-search`:**
  - Language is folded to upper case, the pair refusal is deleted, and the output gains `in_research_scope`.
  - A declared jurisdiction the map doesn't pair is accepted and reported as outside the research scope.
  - An unknown language is still refused.
- **Blocked-reason writers:**
  - `no-quantified-claims` and `superseded` are refused with pointers to `record-scan` and `supersede-source`.
  - `amend-source` may now set the column.
  - `record-scan` clears a block and returns `block_cleared`.
- **`record-scan --text-scope full`:** it refuses a page-less text when the source's logged payload states a page range, and names the range.
- **`observe-term --verbatim-exempt`:** it now calls the same `_refuse_exempt_with_body` as `add-extraction`, so there is no second copy of the check.
- **`--ref-id`:** it is optional and computed on `add-source` and `add-locator`. A wrong id given by hand is still refused.

- **Tests it repairs:**
  - `test_run_pipeline_refusals` J02, G02 and E04.
  - The `test_db_amend_writers` fixture that aborted the whole file, so the file must now run to the end.

- **Cases it adds:** it adopts the A1, A2 and A2b acceptance cases into one regression file. Each must be shown failing on pre-round code, or T states why it can't be.

**After T:** the commit and push (a consistent tree), then Unit P (prose, now including the citation-miner and research-log-manager skills), then V (independent replay) and the second antagonist pass.
